custom_Timelock_admin.source: GMX Timelock inherits RoleModule — roles stored in RoleStore (0x3c3d99FD298f679DBC2CEcd132b4eC4d0F5e6e72). Role hashes: keccak256(abi.encode('TIMELOCK_ADMIN'))=0xf49b0c86..., keccak256(abi.encode('TIMELOCK_MULTISIG'))=0xe068a8d8...

members.note: plain EOA — single private key can execute TIMELOCK_ADMIN functions

TIMELOCK_ADMIN.finding: 2 of 4 TIMELOCK_ADMIN holders are plain EOAs. TIMELOCK_ADMIN can execute timelock admin functions (increaseTimelockDelay, setOracleProviderForToken, grantRole) with a single key. No multisig protection for these two holders.
TIMELOCK_ADMIN.source: getRoleMemberCount(TIMELOCK_ADMIN)=4, getRoleMembers(0,4)=[4 addresses]. getThreshold() on each to determine type.

key_permissioned_functions: DataStore.setUint/setInt/setAddress/setBool/setBytes32/setString/setBytes(...) x39 — modifier: onlyController (CONTROLLER role in RoleStore)
new_discoveries: Custom Timelock uses two distinct roles: onlyTimelockMultisig (propose/signal) and onlyTimelockAdmin (execute/finalize). These are NOT standard OZ roles.
onlyTimelockMultisig holder: NOT resolved on-chain (gov()/owner()/timelockAdmin() revert on non-OZ interface). Requires event scan or Etherscan to identify.
onlyTimelockAdmin holder: NOT resolved on-chain. Same blocker.
DataStore is the central permission gate: all 39 setters gated by onlyController (= CONTROLLER role in RoleStore). Keeper bots hold CONTROLLER.
manual_observations: RoleStore controls all role-based access. CONTROLLER role gives full protocol access.
GovTimelockController (1-day delay) is the governance path for on-chain changes.
Custom Timelock (1-day delay): signals require onlyTimelockMultisig, finalization requires onlyTimelockAdmin. Two-key scheme for critical operations.
No proxy upgrade pattern detected — contracts appear non-upgradeable (direct deployments per GitHub).

can_user_exit_unilaterally.source: GM token withdrawal requires keeper execution (ExchangeRouter.createWithdrawal → keeper executes via WithdrawalHandler). Users CAN cancel pending requests (cancelWithdrawal), recovering tokens. But actual exit from positions requires keeper liveness. If keeper down, user can cancel but cannot execute their own withdrawal.

exit_function_candidate.value: cancelWithdrawal(bytes32) on ExchangeRouter for pending request recovery; createWithdrawal() + keeper for actual exit
exit_function_candidate.source: GMX v2 architecture docs + contract ABI

exit_depends_on.source: Keeper bots (CONTROLLER role in RoleStore) required to execute withdrawals. Users cannot self-execute withdrawal orders.

forced_inclusion.source: GMX v2 is a dApp on Arbitrum One, not a rollup. N/A for forced inclusion.

lp_exit.mechanism: createWithdrawal() on ExchangeRouter → keeper executes via WithdrawalHandler. Users cannot self-execute.
lp_exit.permission_gate: CONTROLLER role (keeper bots) required to execute withdrawals via WithdrawalHandler
lp_exit.censorship_resistance: cancelWithdrawal(bytes32) allows user to recover pending withdrawal request collateral if keeper doesn't execute. But actual exit from GM tokens requires keeper liveness.
lp_exit.source: Scanner: DataStore 39 setters onlyController. Architecture confirmed via GitHub deployments + ExchangeRouter.dataStore() on-chain.

trader_exit.mechanism: createOrder()/cancelOrder() on ExchangeRouter. Execution requires ORDER_KEEPER role.
trader_exit.source: Scanner: OrderVault 7 functions onlyController. Keeper required for order execution.
